newsitem.title: ESTONIA: CRESCO, ESCO HOLDINGS BID FOR SHIPPING FIRM.
newsitem.headline: CRESCO, ESCO HOLDINGS BID FOR SHIPPING FIRM.

text.p: Investment house Baltic Cresco confirmed on Thursday that it has placed a joint bid with ESCO Holdings to privatise the Estonian Shipping Company.
"We submitted a joint bid with ESCO Holdings," Olev Schults, project officer with Baltic Cresco, told Reuters.
"The main reason for the joint bid was for a better competitive environment, for a one-on-one competition, and two, because of a natural match of our interests," he added.
The two groups joined efforts for the second round of bidding for 70 percent of Estonian Shipping Company, which closed today at two pm.
The privatisation agency earlier said there were two bids in the second round but would not name the second bidder.
In the first round, the other bidder was a consortium called Arbonale, which included Jinhui Shipping & Transport, Nomura and Norwegian group Marsoft.
Baltic Cresco said it would not release any further detals on its bid at this time.
Baltic Cresco is an Estonian-based investment house which had two key backers in the first round, one a local and the other from the United States.
ESCO holdings, which was also given the right to bid in the second round, included a local consortium and Swedish brokers Carnegie AB.
The Estonian Shipping Company is the largest in Estonia. It has 47 ships, 2,400 employees and share capital of 107.9 million kroons.
It had 21.4 million kroons net profit in the first quarter of this year. Its assets were 1.3 billion kroons at the end of 1996.
